channel.title: Proxly Updates
channel.description: Updates for Proxly - Smart Browser Chooser

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description:
Added

  • Link History: A new History view shows every link Proxly has routed, where it went, and which rule matched
    • Split-view layout with sidebar, search, filtering and date grouping
    • Detail view with metadata cards (rule, browser, match type, source app)
    • In an entry details pane you can click a button to instantly create a rule from it
    • Per-rule “Exclude from History” toggle for sensitive rules
    • Recent history section accessible directly from the menu bar
  • Rule Exclusion Patterns: Each rule can now declare patterns that exclude a URL even when the main domain pattern would have matched it
    • Example: a “Slack” rule matching *.slack.com can exclude auth.slack.com so login flows go to your default browser
    • Patterns support the same wildcard/regex syntax as the main domain pattern
    • Visible inline in the Rule Editor under a dedicated disclosure group
    • Exclusions sync via iCloud and are preserved across import/export
  • Mailto: Link Routing: Open mailto: links with the email client of your choice instead of whatever macOS decided
    • Manage your installed mail apps in Settings with drag-to-reorder and visibility toggles
    • Per-rule mail app selection, alongside browser and native-app targets
    • Email rules show a clear Email badge in the rule list
  • Private Mode for Profiles: Open links in a private/incognito window straight from a rule
    • Toggle on any browser profile in the Rule Editor
    • Hold Option while clicking a browser in the Selection Panel to open privately on-the-fly
    • Works for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox, and Safari (via AppleScript)
  • Short URL Expansion: Shortened URLs (bit.ly, t.co, etc.) are now resolved to their destination before rules are evaluated, so a rule for youtube.com will match a shortened YouTube link too
  • Selection Panel Power-User Features:
    • Full keyboard navigation with wrap-around
    • Cmd+C copies the URL straight from the panel
    • Cmd+click on a browser to instantly create a rule for that domain
    • Option+click for private mode (see above)
  • Usage-Based Browser Sorting: Optional setting that sorts browsers in the picker and panel by how often you actually use them, instead of alphabetically
  • Share Extension & macOS Services: Send links to Proxly from any app via the Share menu or the system Services menu - Proxly will route them through your rules just like a normal link
  • AI Rule Generation in All 7 Languages: The AI rule generator now works in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, and Polish, with multilingual post-processing
    • Natural-language phrases like “everything except work hours” are now also extracted as exclusion patterns
  • JavaScript Transformations Upgraded: For users authoring custom JS transformations:
    • console.log / console.warn / console.error for debugging directly in the JS editor
    • Mutable URL properties - modify href, pathname, host, search directly without rebuilding the URL string
    • SearchParams API for read/write query parameter manipulation
    • Source-app and search-provider context injected as input, so transformations can behave differently for links coming from Slack vs. Mail, or from Google vs. DuckDuckGo
    • Updated in-app help with examples for all new APIs

Changed

  • UI Polish: Hover feedback and spring animations on interactive elements, plus subtle micro-interactions, staggered reveals, and a touch of celebration on key moments to make the app feel more alive
  • Selection Panel Layout: Modifier-key behavior reworked for consistency; the layout no longer shifts when modifiers are held
  • Rule Deduplication: Importing rules that share a domain but target different scheme types (e.g. http vs mailto) no longer flags them as duplicates
  • Tooltips: Comprehensive localized tooltips added across the entire UI in all 7 supported languages

Fixed

  • Short URL Rules: Rule actions now apply to the resolved destination of a short link, not the shortener domain
  • Wrong Browser Profile: Chromium profile detection now uses the on-disk directory name instead of the display name, eliminating cases where the wrong profile would open after a profile rename
  • Profile Cache on Cold Launch: Profile data is warmed at startup, so the first link of the day always routes to the correct profile instead of falling back to the default
  • Safari Profile Selection: Confirming a Safari profile in the rule editor now correctly persists the choice
  • Corrupted Usage Cache: A corrupted browser-usage cache no longer prevents the panel from showing - Proxly clears the bad data and continues
  • Menu Bar Responsiveness: Reduced redundant accessibility work on the menu bar status item for snappier interaction

Security

  • Licensing System Hardened (Standalone build): Major upgrade to license verification - encrypted local storage of license data, atomic activation to prevent drift on flaky networks, signed server responses, and tougher certificate pinning that survives upstream cert rotations without breaking the app. License errors are now also more informative when something goes wrong.
